- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 5–10% of recent mean or add 1–2% lagged volatility buffer.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 1.2x prior peak for 3–5 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias in early 2023 (e.g., 2023-01-24/25) — if 30d forecast is >10% above 18d history mean, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “late-stage lag” — true values often diverge significantly after day 15–20; apply “early correction” rule: if forecast > true by >5% at day 15, reduce by 2–3% per day until day 25.
